units.name: Communication and the patient–doctor relationship
units.rationale: The consultation is the core intervention of general practice. Effective, empathic communication improves accuracy of diagnosis, patient adherence, satisfaction and outcomes, and reduces medico-legal risk.
competencies: Open the consultation, elicit the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations, and close with a clear, mutually agreed plan
Adapt communication to health literacy, culture, language (interpreters) and disability
Break bad news with a structured approach, manage strong emotions and consult safely with children, adolescents and older people
units.case_example: A 45-year-old presents with 'tiredness'. As the consultation unfolds, three separate concerns emerge: her own tiredness, her father's recent cancer diagnosis, and a request for a medical certificate. (CCE areas: data gathering - elicit all three agendas; clinical management - prioritise; communication - agenda-setting, ICE, summarising.)
learning_strategies: Record (with consent) one of your own consultations each week and review it against a consultation model
Practise breaking bad news aloud with a study partner using SPIKES
Ask your supervisor to observe a consultation and give structured feedback

units.name: Applied professional knowledge and skills
units.rationale: The GP applies clinical knowledge through reasoning: history, examination, differential diagnosis, targeted investigation and safe management - the engine room of the KFP and daily practice.
competencies: Take a focused history and perform a relevant, respectful examination
Generate a pragmatic differential diagnosis and choose investigations that change management (avoiding over-investigation)
Interpret results in context, prescribe safely, perform common GP procedures, and manage clinical uncertainty
units.case_example: A 52-year-old has 3 weeks of fatigue. First-line tests show ferritin 12 with normal Hb. (CCE areas: data gathering - menstrual, dietary, GI symptoms; clinical management - iron deficiency needs a cause: coeliac screen, GI malignancy considerations by age/sex; communication - explaining why 'a bit low in iron' still needs investigation.)
learning_strategies: Do 20 AKT questions daily and log error patterns in your mistake log
Case-based discussion with your supervisor on 2 undifferentiated presentations per week
Practise a structured approach to abnormal results (anaemia, LFTs, electrolytes)

units.name: Population health and the context of general practice
units.rationale: GPs deliver preventive care at scale: screening programs, immunisation, notifiable disease management and health equity. Population thinking turns individual consultations into community outcomes.
competencies: Apply epidemiology when offering screening (benefits, harms, intervals)
Run preventive activities systematically (Red Book) and use practice recall systems
Recognise and act on health inequity; manage notifiable conditions and public health risks
units.case_example: A 54-year-old attends for a script refill. Her screening is overdue: bowel, cervical. (CCE areas: data gathering - what she already knows; clinical management - opportunistic offer of iFOBT and CST, immunisation status; communication - prevention in a time-poor consult without lecturing.)
learning_strategies: Audit 10 consecutive patient files for due preventive activities
Memorise current program intervals (cervical 25-74/5-yearly HPV, bowel 45-74/2-yearly iFOBT, BreastScreen 50-74)
Write a one-page practice plan for improving under-screened groups

units.name: Professional and ethical role
units.rationale: Professionalism underpins patient trust: ethical reasoning, confidentiality, consent, duty of candour, and care of the doctor's own health and that of colleagues.
competencies: Apply ethical frameworks to consent, capacity and confidentiality dilemmas
Meet mandatory reporting obligations and know the limits of confidentiality
Maintain own health, recognise colleague impairment, and practise within competence
units.case_example: A colleague at your practice seems increasingly withdrawn and smells of alcohol at morning tea. (CCE areas: clinical management - patient safety duties, doctors' health pathways, mandatory notification thresholds; communication - the supportive colleague conversation; professionalism - documentation.)
learning_strategies: Discuss 2 ethics vignettes per fortnight with a study group
Learn your state's mandatory reporting and child protection numbers by heart
Complete an AHPRA code-of-conduct self-review

guidelines.title: Medical Board - Good medical practice code

units.name: Organisational and legal dimensions
units.rationale: Safe general practice runs on systems: records, results handling, prescribing safety, privacy, employment law and quality improvement. Organisational failures - not knowledge failures - cause much preventable harm.
competencies: Keep contemporaneous, adequate records; apply privacy principles and appropriate confidentiality
Run safe results and recall systems; manage referrals and prescribing within MBS/PBS rules
Know key legal duties: certification, driving fitness, mandatory reporting, and respond to incidents openly
units.case_example: A patient telephones: 'Did anyone get my biopsy result? I had it 6 weeks ago.' No result was ever actioned. (CCE areas: clinical management - open disclosure, urgent retrieval and clinical assessment; professionalism - incident reporting and system fix; communication - the honest, apologetic conversation.)
learning_strategies: Do a mock audit of your practice's results-tracking system
Learn the common MBS item numbers used weekly in your practice
Practise writing one defensible referral letter and one certificate per week

units.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health
units.rationale: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples experience a burden of disease 2-3 times the non-Indigenous rate, with earlier onset chronic disease. Culturally safe, high-trust general practice closes gaps: annual health checks, earlier risk assessment, CTG scripts and working with community-controlled services.
competencies: Deliver culturally safe care: ask about identification respectfully, build trust, understand institutional barriers and intergenerational trauma
Deliver the annual 715 health check and Close the Gap PBS entitlements; start CVD risk assessment from 35 and diabetes screening earlier
Work with ATSI community-controlled health services and local referral pathways; support patient self-determination
units.case_example: A 52-year-old Aboriginal man presents with tiredness; HbA1c returns 7.2%. His father died of kidney disease. He is wary of hospitals. (CCE areas: data gathering - family history, previous screening; clinical management - confirm diagnosis, cycle of care, CTG entitlements, vaccination; communication - plain language, trust, service choice.)
learning_strategies: Complete RACGP ATSI health activity on gplearning
Learn the 715, CTG script and follow-up item numbers cold
Visit or arrange a visit to your local ATSI community-controlled health service

guidelines.title: National guide to preventive healthcare for ATSI people (3rd ed)
Australian Institute of Health and Welfare - ATSI health reports

units.name: Rural health
units.rationale: Rural GPs work with extended scope, greater distance from specialist services and different workforce realities: telehealth, retrieval, and managing emergencies that urban colleagues refer out.
competencies: Stabilise and coordinate emergencies with longer transfer times; know local retrieval pathways
Use telehealth effectively and coordinate care across distances
Manage the professional isolation and on-call realities of rural practice; maintain skills and self-care
units.case_example: You are the only doctor in a small town. A 60-year-old collapses with chest pain; the nearest PCI hospital is 90 minutes by road. (CCE areas: data gathering - ECG, history in parallel with treatment; clinical management - pre-hospital STEMI pathway, aspirin, GTN, oxygen if hypoxic, 000/retrieval; communication - calm coordination, family updates.)
learning_strategies: Rehearse your practice's emergency drug trolley and anaphylaxis/STEMI/stroke workflows
Complete a rural emergency skills course (or refresh) if applicable to your scope
Write out your local after-hours and retrieval phone tree

units.name: Abuse and violence
units.rationale: Family and domestic violence affects about 1 in 4 women presenting to general practice; GPs are often the first and sometimes the only professional a victim discloses to. Recognition, safety assessment and patient-paced response save lives; child safety obligations run alongside.
competencies: Ask directly and privately, believe, validate, and assess immediate safety including strangulation risk
Safety-plan, document meticulously (verbatim, body maps), and connect to FDV services; never force leaving
Meet mandatory child protection obligations when children are exposed
units.case_example: A 38-year-old woman discloses ongoing violence from her partner; she is not ready to leave. Two children at home. (CCE areas: data gathering - privacy, pattern, strangulation, children; clinical management - safety assessment, safety plan, 1800RESPECT, child protection duty; communication - patient-paced, non-directive.)
learning_strategies: Read the RACGP White Book end-to-end once; re-read the safety assessment chapter
Practise the first-response script aloud: validation without pressure
Memorise local FDV services, the Elder Abuse helpline and Child Safety number

guidelines.title: RACGP White Book - Abuse and violence

materials.label: QLD Domestic Violence Protection Act resources / DV Connect

units.name: Addiction medicine
units.rationale: Alcohol, tobacco and other drug problems are among the highest-burden conditions GPs manage. Brief interventions work; pharmacotherapies (smoking, opioid, alcohol) are GP-deliverable; withdrawal states are medical emergencies in the dependent.
competencies: Screen with AUDIT-C and deliver brief intervention for alcohol and smoking (Ask-Advise-Help)
Manage alcohol withdrawal risk (CIWA-Ar, thiamine before glucose) and opioid dependence (buprenorphine/methadone pathways)
Prescribe pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation (varenicline first-line, combination NRT) and reduce harms for all substance use
units.case_example: A 50-year-old drinks 80 g/day and is booked for surgery next week. (CCE areas: data gathering - quantity, withdrawal history, past seizures/delirium; clinical management - withdrawal risk stratification, thiamine, hospital liaison; communication - motivation without confrontation.)
learning_strategies: Learn the alcohol withdrawal ladder and thiamine rules cold
Do the RACGP smoking cessation module; memorise varenicline dosing and cautions
Write out the opioid substitution pathway in your state

units.name: Cardiovascular health
units.rationale: CVD is Australia's leading cause of death: 26% of all deaths. GPs control the levers - absolute risk assessment, BP, lipids, anticoagulation in AF, and post-event secondary prevention. ATSI adults carry double the mortality, with risk assessment from 35.
competencies: Assess and manage absolute CVD risk (Aus CVD Risk Calculator; treat risk, not single numbers)
Diagnose and manage hypertension (confirm out-of-office), AF (CHA2DS2-VA anticoagulation), and heart failure (quadruple therapy)
Recognise and refer ACS, aortic dissection and severe valve disease emergently; run post-ACS secondary prevention
units.case_example: A 62-year-old has 2 hours of central chest pain in your practice. ECG: ST elevation V2-V4. (CCE areas: data gathering - focused pain history, risk factors in parallel; clinical management - 000, aspirin 300, GTN if BP allows, PCI transfer; communication - calm urgency, family informed.)
learning_strategies: Master the 2023 CVD risk guideline thresholds and the AF anticoagulation decision
Write the HFrEF quadruple therapy from memory weekly until automatic
Rehearse the practice STEMI/anaphylaxis drill

units.name: Child and youth health
units.rationale: Children are a large share of GP presentations: infections, development, behaviour, and adolescent health. Weight and height are vital signs; fever management is risk-stratified; safeguarding duties run through everything.
competencies: Assess the febrile child by risk (traffic-light); manage common conditions per RCH guidelines (bronchiolitis, croup, otitis media)
Track growth and development; recognise autism/ADHD and refer via correct pathways
Consult adolescents headssfully: confidentiality and its limits; mandatory reporting for abuse
units.case_example: A 6-month-old has fever 38.8 for 24 hours, alert and drinking. (CCE areas: data gathering - traffic-light features; clinical management - green category, safety-netting, no antibiotics; communication - clear when-to-return advice.)
learning_strategies: Learn the fever traffic-light table and the under-3-months rule cold
Bookmark RCH CPGs; do the bronchiolitis, croup, and gastro guidelines end-to-end
Do one HEADSS practice consultation with a teen in your clinic this month

units.name: Dermatological presentations
units.rationale: Skin problems are ~15% of GP presentations and Australia has the world's highest skin cancer rates. The GP is the front line for melanoma detection, eczema/psoriasis management and skin surgery decisions.
competencies: Describe lesions systematically; biopsy correctly (excision for suspected melanoma - never shave)
Manage eczema (steroid ladder, emollients, bleach baths), psoriasis (topical combinations, referral criteria), acne (stepwise, isotretinoin rules)
Perform skin checks and recognise high-risk patients; know referral criteria for lesions and wounds
units.case_example: A 40-year-old asks review of a 7 mm changing pigmented lesion on his back with varied colours. (CCE areas: data gathering - ABCD/E, change, risk factors; clinical management - excision biopsy 2 mm margin, dermoscopy where trained; communication - explaining why 'just removing it' must be done properly.)
learning_strategies: Practise describing 10 lesions aloud using formal morphology language
Memorise biopsy margins and which lesions never to shave
Do a dermoscopy basics module if available locally

units.name: Disability care
units.rationale: People with disability face the greatest health inequities: undiagnosed pain, missed prevention, diagnostic overshadowing. The GP's job is ordinary excellent care, delivered accessibly, plus NDIS literacy.
competencies: Deliver annual health assessments for patients with intellectual/physical disability with reasonable adjustments
Communicate with AAC users, carers and support workers; assess capacity decision-by-decision
Navigate the NDIS: reports, allied health coordination, and advocacy for health needs
units.case_example: A 25-year-old woman with cerebral palsy and intellectual disability presents with new agitation; her support worker says 'she's always like this'. (CCE areas: data gathering - pain/constipation/reflux/UTI as equal possibilities, obtaining history from multiple sources; clinical management - treat the cause, not the behaviour; communication - direct address, capacity respect.)
learning_strategies: Read the RACGP position on care of patients with disability
Learn the health assessment item numbers for patients with disability
Audit 5 files of patients with disability for missed prevention

guidelines.title: RACGP - health of people with disabilities

units.name: Disaster health
units.rationale: GPs are embedded in every disaster response - fires, floods, pandemics: continuity of care for the vulnerable, public health measures, and practice business continuity.
competencies: Maintain care continuity for high-risk patients during disruption (medication supply, telehealth)
Apply public health directions and outbreak principles; know your role and limits in activation
Plan practice continuity: records access, remote work, staff safety
units.case_example: A flood has cut power to your practice for 3 days; several patients on insulin and warfarin are stranded without medication. (CCE areas: data gathering - identify the vulnerable cohort; clinical management - alternative supply, relocation of care; professionalism - proactive outreach.)
learning_strategies: Write a one-page practice continuity plan for your top 3 local risks
Complete an emergency/incident management module

units.name: Doctors' health
units.rationale: Doctors have elevated rates of mental illness, substance use and suicide, and are notoriously poor patients. Confidential, doctor-to-doctor care pathways exist; the treating doctor generally does NOT face mandatory notification for treating impairment.
competencies: Encourage every doctor to have their own GP; provide non-judgemental care to colleagues
Recognise burnout, depression, substance use in self and colleagues; intervene supportively early
Know doctors' health services (drs4drs) and the boundaries of the treating-physician notification exemption
units.case_example: A 29-year-old intern confesses to 6+ drinks nightly to sleep, plus zopiclone from a sample pack, terrified of exposure. (CCE areas: data gathering - severity, risk, work impact; clinical management - safer sleep plan, alcohol taper, doctors' health service, own GP; professionalism - confidentiality within legal limits.)
learning_strategies: Save the Doctors' Health Service number in your phone now
Read the treating-practitioner exemption rules once carefully

units.name: Ear, nose, throat and oral health
units.rationale: ENT complaints fill waiting rooms: otitis media (watchful waiting criteria), sore throat (Centor), sinusitis, hearing loss, epistaxis first aid, and oral lesions with cancer red flags.
competencies: Manage AOM with analgesia-first and defined antibiotic triggers; treat otitis externa topically
Triage sore throat (Centor, penicillin), sinusitis (>10 days worsening), and epistaxis (pressure first-line)
Assess hearing loss (Rinne/Weber patterns) and refer; recognise non-healing oral ulcers (3 weeks) urgently
units.case_example: A 2-year-old with bilateral AOM, 48 hours, distressed but systemically well. (CCE areas: data gathering - analgesia adequacy, red flags; clinical management - delayed prescribing/watchful waiting; communication - what to watch for, when to return.)
learning_strategies: Memorise AOM immediate-antibiotic criteria and the 3-week oral ulcer rule
Practise Rinne/Weber interpretation on 5 cases

units.name: Education in general practice
units.rationale: Teaching is a core professional role: supervising students and registrars, giving feedback, and teaching patients. Good teaching improves the whole practice's care.
competencies: Give structured feedback (set-readiness, observe, debrief)
Teach in the consultation efficiently (One-Minute Preceptor, SNAPPS)
Support learners in difficulty and manage the failing student fairly
units.case_example: A final-year student presents a case badly; you have a full waiting room. (CCE areas: clinical management - model efficient teaching; professionalism - feedback culture; communication - educational alliance.)
learning_strategies: Practise the One-Minute Preencer structure three times this week

units.name: Emergency medicine
units.rationale: GP surgeries are unplanned-care sites: anaphylaxis, sepsis, ACS, stroke, trauma and collapse all walk through the door. Outcomes depend on recognition, first-line treatment and timely transfer.
competencies: Deliver IM adrenaline for anaphylaxis (0.5 mg adult, thigh, repeat 5 min) and salbutamol/steroids for severe asthma
Recognise sepsis (qSOFA) and stroke (FAST); transfer 000 with pre-alert
Run a practice emergency trolley: adrenaline, salbutamol, GTN, aspirin, glucometer, defibrillator
units.case_example: A patient collapses anaphylactic after an antibiotic injection in your treatment room. (CCE areas: clinical management - IM adrenaline, call 000, lie flat, IV access; communication - team leadership, family; professionalism - incident documentation.)
learning_strategies: Run a team anaphylaxis drill this month; restock the trolley
Write your top-10 surgery emergency protocols on one card

units.name: Endocrine and metabolic health
units.rationale: Diabetes, obesity, thyroid and lipids dominate chronic GP care and exam blueprints equally. Modern management is comorbidity-driven (SGLT2i/GLP-1) and complication-screened (annual cycle).
competencies: Diagnose and manage T2DM: individualised HbA1c, comorbidity-based drug choice, annual complications screen
Interpret thyroid function tests and manage overt/subclinical disease, including pregnancy
Manage obesity as a chronic disease (5-10% goals, pharmacotherapy criteria) and lipids by absolute risk/FH rules
units.case_example: A 60-year-old with T2DM (HbA1c 8.5%), eGFR 62, on metformin and gliclazide, smokes. (CCE areas: data gathering - cycle-of-care gaps; clinical management - SGLT2i add-on, BP/lipid targets, smoking; communication - prioritising with the patient.)
learning_strategies: Write the T2DM cycle of care and drug-choice ladder from memory weekly
Master TFT interpretation including pregnancy and subclinical patterns

units.name: Eye presentations
units.rationale: Sight-threatening emergencies present to GPs first: chemical injury (irrigate first), contact-lens keratitis, acute angle closure, retinal detachment, and GCA-related vision loss. Also: diabetic retinopathy screening and red-eye triage.
competencies: Irrigate chemical burns immediately (30 min) before anything else; assess pH
Triage the red eye: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lenses = same-day ophthalmology
Organise diabetic retinal screening and recognise glaucoma risk opportunistically
units.case_example: A 25-year-old contact-lens wearer has a painful red eye with photophobia and reduced vision. (CCE areas: data gathering - lens habits, overnight wear; clinical management - same-day ophthalmology, no patching, stop lenses; communication - sight-loss seriousness.)
learning_strategies: Print the red-eye triage table and the chemical-injury protocol for your desk
Learn the four sight-threatening headaches of the eye (angle closure, GCA, keratitis, detachment)

units.name: Gastrointestinal health
units.rationale: GI symptoms are among the most common presentations: dyspepsia with alarm features, liver disease (MASLD, viral hepatitis), bowel screening positives, coeliac, IBS and iron deficiency.
competencies: Triage dysphagia/weight loss/anaemia urgently (scope, not PPI trials); manage GORD stepwise
Work up abnormal LFTs systematically (pattern, viral serology, iron, ultrasound, FIB-4)
Manage positive iFOBT (colonoscopy), coeliac (test before diet), and IBS positively (Rome IV, diet)
units.case_example: A 52-year-old asymptomatic man has ALT 95, BMI 33, negative serology. (CCE areas: data gathering - alcohol, meds, risk factors; clinical management - MASLD pathway: confirm, viral/iron/autoimmune screen, FIB-4; communication - fatty liver explanation and prognosis factors.)
learning_strategies: Learn the LFT pattern approach and FIB-4 thresholds
Memorise upper-GI alarm features and the iFOBT-positive action

materials.label: Bowel Screening Program resources for GPs

units.name: Haematological presentations
units.rationale: Anaemia, abnormal clotting and blood count abnormalities are bread-and-butter GP interpretation; anticoagulation decisions and malignancy recognition (blasts, unexplained cytopenias) are high-stakes.
competencies: Classify anaemia by MCV and reticulocytes; find the cause (iron deficiency in adults = find the source)
Anticoagulate appropriately (DOAC-first for AF/VTE; renal dosing, perioperative rules) and set VTE durations by provocation
Recognise haematological emergencies: blasts on film, platelets <20, neutropenic fever - same-day haematology
units.case_example: A 63-year-old man has Hb 102, ferritin 8, microcytic. (CCE areas: data gathering - GI symptoms, diet, family history; clinical management - bidirectional endoscopy, iron replacement 3 months beyond normalisation; communication - why men need the scope.)
learning_strategies: Drill the anaemia grid (micro/macro/normocytic) and iron rules
Learn DOAC perioperative holding and the provoked vs unprovoked VTE durations

units.name: Infectious diseases
units.rationale: GPs prescribe most antibiotics in Australia: stewardship, first-line choices and notifiable disease duties sit with us. Add QLD-specific exposures (Q fever, melioidosis up north) and the returned traveller.
competencies: Choose antibiotics per eTG (UTI nitrofurantoin, cellulitis flucloxacillin, pneumonia amoxycillin) and de-escalate
Diagnose and manage influenza, pertussis, TB risk, and febrile travellers (malaria same-day)
Vaccinate per AIH including catch-ups; manage notifiable diseases and contact advice
units.case_example: A 46-year-old abattoir worker has 5 days of fever and headache in rural QLD. (CCE areas: data gathering - occupation, animals, travel; clinical management - Q fever: doxycycline, serology, notification; communication - occupational implications.)
learning_strategies: Build a personal top-15 antibiotic table with doses and durations
Learn the notifiable diseases list and your public health unit contact

units.name: Integrative medicine
units.rationale: Many patients use complementary medicine: GPs must ask (half don't tell), check interactions, and communicate respectfully about evidence without destroying the relationship.
competencies: Ask routinely about all supplements and practitioners; document
Check for interactions (warfarin/DOACs + fish oils, St John's wort with everything)
Communicate evidence differences honestly; support safe choices, caution on harm
units.case_example: A patient on warfarin starts high-dose fish oil and ginkgo bought online, and her INR becomes erratic. (CCE areas: data gathering - full supplement list; clinical management - interaction management, INR safety net; communication - non-judgemental negotiation.)
learning_strategies: Memorise the top-10 herbal-drug interactions

units.name: Justice system health
units.rationale: Prisoners and forensic patients have worse health than the general population; GPs working in or adjacent to the justice system manage high mental health, substance and chronic disease burdens with confidentiality subtleties.
competencies: Deliver equivalent care to people in custody; recognise the health consequences of incarceration
Manage confidentiality within justice-system constraints (security present at consults)
Coordinate with justice health services on release: continuity scripts, opioid programs
units.case_example: A man recently released from prison needs ongoing methadone, hepatitis C treatment and housing support. (CCE areas: data gathering - custody history, meds, risks; clinical management - DAA treatment, OST continuity, referrals; communication - trust and reintegration.)
learning_strategies: Read one overview of prison health in Australia
Learn the Medicare rules for custodial settings

units.name: Kidney and urinary health
units.rationale: CKD is silent, common and manageable in primary care: eGFR + ACR staging, RAAS blockade, SGLT2i and nephrotoxin avoidance change trajectories. Haematuria and LUTS triage are daily GP work.
competencies: Stage CKD (eGFR + ACR) and manage: BP, RAAS blockade with albuminuria, SGLT2i, sick-day rules
Triage haematuria: visible = urological malignancy pathway; glomerular pattern = nephrology
Manage UTI (nitrofurantoin first), stones, and LUTS stepwise; refer per criteria
units.case_example: A 68-year-old man, eGFR 38 and stable, has a gout flare asking for naproxen. (CCE areas: data gathering - meds, CKD stage; clinical management - NSAID avoidance, topical first, colchicine dose-adjusted; communication - analgesia explanation in CKD.)
learning_strategies: Memorise CKD stages + referral criteria and the sick-day drug list
Learn haematuria triage cold (visible vs glomerular)

guidelines.title: Kidney Health Australia - CKD in primary care

materials.label: CKD management in primary care handbook

units.name: Men's health
units.rationale: Men die younger and attend less: GP opportunities concentrate in chronic disease, mental health and suicide prevention, urological symptoms and ED as a cardiovascular flag.
competencies: Use ED as a CVD screening prompt (assess risk before sildenafil)
Counsel on PSA with informed decision-making (benefits/harms; no population program)
Screen opportunistically: BP, lipids, glucose, mental health in every male consult you can
units.case_example: A 56-year-old smoker with ED requests 'just a script for Viagra'. (CCE areas: data gathering - CVD risk factors, morning erections, mood; clinical management - risk assessment first, PDE5i with nitrate check; communication - reframing ED as a heart check.)
learning_strategies: Learn the PSA conversation (screening vs informed choice) thoroughly
Rehearse asking men about mood and suicide risk directly

units.name: Mental health
units.rationale: Mental illness is the third-largest burden of disease in Australia; GPs deliver most mental health care. Depression, anxiety, bipolar, psychosis, perinatal disorders and suicide risk are core GP competencies.
competencies: Screen (PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS, K10), assess suicide risk directly (plan/means/intent), and safety-plan (never contracts)
Deliver stepped care: psychological therapy +/- SSRI with structured review (2 weeks tolerability, 4-6 response)
Recognise bipolar/psychosis early and refer; manage perinatal and youth mental health within pathways
units.case_example: A 35-year-old woman with PHQ-9 = 18 has passive death wishes but no plan; two children at home. (CCE areas: data gathering - direct risk questions, protective factors, substances; clinical management - safety plan, same-week review, SSRI, referral; communication - hope, control, follow-through.)
learning_strategies: Learn a suicide risk framework you can say out loud in 60 seconds
Memorise the MH referral options in your area (mental health plan, crisis lines)

units.name: Migrant, refugee and asylum seeker health
units.rationale: New arrivals carry specific health needs: refugee screening bundles, interpreter-mediated care, torture/trauma awareness, and visa-status effects on Medicare access.
competencies: Use professional interpreters always (TIS), speak to the patient, and confirm dialect
Deliver arrival screening: hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis, TB, parasites; vaccinate and catch up
Practise trauma-informed care: never force disclosure; navigate Medicare/visa issues kindly
units.case_example: A 28-year-old pregnant refugee from Africa, no English, first antenatal visit. (CCE areas: data gathering - interpreter, obstetric, exposure country; clinical management - booking labs + hep B/HIV/syphilis, TB screen, parasite screen; communication - teach-back, safety.)
learning_strategies: Save the TIS Doctors line number; practise booking one
Learn the refugee screening bundle by heart

units.name: Military and veteran health
units.rationale: Veterans carry distinct risks: PTSD, moral injury, hearing loss, musculoskeletal injury and higher suicide rates. DVA arrangements and veteran-aware care improve engagement.
competencies: Recognise service-related conditions (PTSD presentations, hearing, chronic pain) and ask about service history
Navigate DVA funding: gold/white card entitlements and GP items
Coordinate veteran mental health care with Open Arms and specialist services
units.case_example: A 45-year-old ex-serviceman has insomnia, irritability and heavy drinking since deployment. (CCE areas: data gathering - service history, PTSD screen, alcohol; clinical management - veteran-specific pathways, DVA, Open Arms; communication - trust, no assumptions.)
learning_strategies: Learn the DVA card types and what they cover

units.name: Musculoskeletal presentations
units.rationale: MSK complaints are the most common reason for GP visits: backs, knees, shoulders, arthritis. Red flags first, imaging restraint second, function-focused management third.
competencies: Screen back pain red flags (cauda equina, cancer, infection, fracture) and manage most acute back pain without imaging
Manage OA (exercise/weight loss first), gout (acute + ULT rules: start low, titrate to urate <0.30, prophylaxis), and RA (early referral)
Assess injuries by structure (Ottawa rules); know when to image, inject, refer
units.case_example: A 34-year-old man has acute low back pain after lifting; no red flags. (CCE areas: data gathering - red flag screen; clinical management - stay active, heat, analgesia, no MRI; communication - reassurance and expected course.)
learning_strategies: Memorise the back-pain red flag list and Ottawa ankle rules
Learn allopurinol start-titrate-prophylaxis rules and the PMR/GCA pair

units.name: Neurological presentations
units.rationale: Headache, dizziness, stroke, seizures and dementia are high-yield GP neurology: pattern recognition separates benign from urgent, and time matters in stroke care.
competencies: Triage headache red flags (thunderclap, fever, neurology, >50y new, GCA) and manage migraine with correct prophylaxis triggers
Manage dizziness by pattern (BPPV: Dix-Hallpike/Epley) and recognise posterior circulation strokes
Respond to TIA/seizure correctly (same-day TIA assessment; driving rules) and structure dementia workup (reversible causes)
units.case_example: A 70-year-old has 20 minutes of arm weakness yesterday; resolved today, feels well. (CCE areas: data gathering - deficit detail, risk factors; clinical management - same-day TIA pathway, ABCD2 not for triage in Australia, aspirin per pathway; communication - urgency despite feeling well.)
learning_strategies: Write the headache red-flag list and the TIA same-day rule on a card
Practise Dix-Hallpike/Epley on a colleague

units.name: Occupational and environmental medicine
units.rationale: Work drives health and health drives work capacity: certificates, return-to-work plans, occupational disease recognition (dermatitis, Q fever, noise) and environmental exposures.
competencies: Certify accurately (what you can verify); write return-to-work plans with specific duties
Recognise occupational disease patterns (wet-work dermatitis, zoonoses, solvents) and link exposure to diagnosis
Understand workers' compensation systems and the GP's reporting role
units.case_example: A 34-year-old hairdresser has hand dermatitis worse on workdays. (CCE areas: data gathering - exposure inventory, gloves, wet work; clinical management - allergen avoidance, topical ladder, notification for compensation; communication - work modification negotiation.)
learning_strategies: Learn certificate-writing rules and your state's workers comp process

units.name: Older persons' health
units.rationale: Frailty, multimorbidity and polypharmacy define care of older people: annual health assessments, deprescribing, falls, cognition and elder abuse. The aim is function and dignity, not number-chasing.
competencies: Deliver comprehensive geriatric assessment (75+ health assessment): function, falls, cognition, mood, meds, social
Deprescribe systematically (fall-risk drugs, anticholinergics, PPIs without indication); individualise BP/HbA1c targets
Recognise delirium (acute = cause hunt), elder abuse, and drive advance care planning early
units.case_example: An 85-year-old has 3 falls in 6 months on temazepam and doxazosin with postural drop. (CCE areas: data gathering - meds, home hazards, vision, strength; clinical management - deprescribe first, exercise, vitamin D if deficient; communication - goals-of-care conversation.)
learning_strategies: Write the frailty-aware target list (when to relax BP/HbA1c)
Learn the 4 AT delirium screen and the multifactorial falls pathway

materials.label: Silver Book (Medical care of older persons)

units.name: Pain management
units.rationale: Persistent pain is a disease in its own right. Opioid harm taught Australia that biopsychosocial, function-first care is the only approach that works.
competencies: Assess pain biopsychosocially (function, mood, sleep, beliefs, context)
Manage acute pain well (multimodal, short courses) to prevent chronicity; taper high-dose opioids with support
Deliver interdisciplinary persistent pain care (programs, pacing, CBT) rather than escalating drugs
units.case_example: A 47-year-old on oxycodone 40 mg/day for chronic back pain asks for more. (CCE areas: data gathering - function, mood, aberrant behaviours; clinical management - explain hyperalgesia, taper plan, interdisciplinary program; communication - alliance without capitulation.)
learning_strategies: Learn the opioid taper structure and the yellow-flag screen

units.name: Palliative care
units.rationale: Most Australians die with diseases GPs manage. Good end-of-life care: symptom control, anticipatory prescribing, recognising dying, carer support and voluntary assisted dying literacy (QLD law since 2023).
competencies: Manage terminal symptoms: pain (1/6 breakthrough rule), dyspnoea, secretions, delirium, nausea - anticipatory SC sets
Recognise the dying phase and communicate it honestly; coordinate home/RACF deaths
Facilitate advance care planning and know QLD VAD law (eligibility, process, conscientious objection)
units.case_example: A 78-year-old with metastatic lung cancer at home is entering the dying phase; family anxious. (CCE areas: data gathering - symptoms, fears, supports; clinical management - anticipatory meds, care team, cessation of burdensome interventions; communication - what dying looks like, permission for family.)
learning_strategies: Write the anticipatory drug set (drug/indication/dose) from memory weekly
Read the QLD VAD eligibility summary once

units.name: Pregnancy and reproductive health
units.rationale: GPs do most antenatal and postnatal care: booking, routine screening, shared care, and the urgent triage points (ectopic, pre-eclampsia, reduced movements). Contraception and preconception counselling are core GP craft.
competencies: Deliver first antenatal visit care: dating, booking bloods (group/Ab, FBE, hep B, HIV, syphilis, urine MC&S), screening options discussion
Recognise and refer: ectopic (pain/bleeding + positive test), pre-eclampsia red flags, reduced movements >26 weeks
Provide full contraception counselling (LARC-first, UKMEC) and postnatal care (EPDS, feeding, contraception timing)
units.case_example: A 31-year-old at 9 weeks books in; partner from a high hepatitis B prevalence country. (CCE areas: data gathering - medical, family, exposure history; clinical management - booking tests + extra risk-based, folate/iodine, screening discussion; communication - informed choices.)
learning_strategies: Write the booking blood list and the pre-eclampsia red flags cold
Learn UKMEC categories for the top 5 contraceptives

units.name: Research in general practice
units.rationale: Evidence-literate GPs appraise studies, run audits and sometimes contribute research. Critical appraisal keeps practice honest; audit improves it.
competencies: Appraise studies: design, validity, size, applicability to your patients
Run clinical audits (SNAP, prescribing, prevention) and act on findings
Contribute data/answering surveys where useful; understand basic ethics processes
units.case_example: A drug rep presents a new trial showing '30% relative risk reduction'. (CCE areas: data gathering - absolute vs relative risk; clinical management - applicability to your population; professionalism - evidence over marketing.)
learning_strategies: Do one critical appraisal exercise on a paper in your field per month
Join or form a journal club

units.name: Respiratory health
units.rationale: Asthma and COPD alone affect ~2.5 million Australians; GPs manage both from diagnosis to palliative. SABA-only asthma treatment is now history; spirometry is mandatory for COPD diagnosis.
competencies: Diagnose asthma (variability + reversibility) and step to ICS-formoterol AIR therapy; written action plans; review reliever overuse
Diagnose COPD with post-bronchodilator spirometry; deliver the only trajectory-changers (cessation, rehab) and step-up rules
Triage haemoptysis (urgent CT + respiratory referral for smokers/mass) and investigate chronic cough systematically
units.case_example: A 24-year-old uses salbutamol 3-4 times weekly for months. (CCE areas: data gathering - control assessment, triggers, technique; clinical management - ICS-formoterol, action plan; communication - why the blue inhaler alone is no longer OK.)
learning_strategies: Learn the AIR algorithm and the COPD step-up criteria (eosinophils >=0.3 / 2 exacerbations)
Do spirometry interpretation drills weekly

units.name: Sexual health and gender diversity
units.rationale: STI rates are rising in Australia; GPs do most testing and all partner notification duties. Affirming care for LGBTQI+ patients measurably improves their health engagement.
competencies: Test by site and risk (NAATs, serology); treat per Australian STI guidelines and arrange partner notification
Provide PrEP/PEP (PEP within 72 h) and HIV care linkage; screen opportunistically in every eligible patient
Deliver gender-affirming, non-judgemental care; use chosen names/pronouns; know referral pathways
units.case_example: A 22-year-old asymptomatic man who has sex with men requests a check. (CCE areas: data gathering - sexual history without judgement; clinical management - site-specific NAATs + HIV/syphilis, PrEP discussion; communication - normalising, confidentiality.)
learning_strategies: Memorise the site-by-site STI testing table
Save the PEP hotline and PrEP guidelines link

units.name: Travel medicine
units.rationale: Pre-travel consults are risk assessments: destination-specific vaccines (typhoid, hep A, rabies, Japanese encephalitis), malaria chemoprophylaxis, and behaviour advice. Returned travellers are a different consult.
competencies: Assess by itinerary: vaccines by destination, malaria risk by region and season, dengue/Zika advice
Prescribe chemoprophylaxis correctly (drug, start-before, side-effects) and give bite-avoidance advice
Manage the returned traveller: fever same-day (malaria), persistent diarrhoea, eosinophilia
units.case_example: A family with two children is trekking in rural Thailand for 3 weeks. (CCE areas: data gathering - itinerary, activities, duration, pregnancy/medical; clinical management - routine + travel vaccines, malaria assessment, bite avoidance; communication - risk without alarm.)
learning_strategies: Build a region quick-table for the 5 most common destinations your patients visit

units.name: Women's health
units.rationale: Cervical screening (self-collection era), menopause care, HMB, PCOS and breast symptoms are daily GP work. Individualised, evidence-based care - especially around MHT - is the standard.
competencies: Deliver cervical screening including self-collection choice; manage results per pathways (LBC after non-16/18 HPV)
Manage menopause: individualised MHT risk-benefit (timing hypothesis), non-hormonal options, GSM treatments
Assess breast lumps urgently (triple assessment pathway) and manage HMB/PCOS systematically
units.case_example: A 49-year-old with perimenopausal symptoms and a uterus asks about 'natural' hormones. (CCE areas: data gathering - symptom inventory, risk factors; clinical management - MHT options/risks, compounded hormones caution; communication - shared decision, contraception still needed.)
learning_strategies: Learn the cervical screening result pathway and MHT contraindications
Read the menopause society statement on compounded bioidenticals once
